data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A large service with strictly more internal redundancy is more resilient because it transforms 'correlated failures' into 'manageable state transitions' via global telemetry and rapid rollback.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The control plane itself is the source of the correlated failure (e.g., a buggy global config push).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The recovery mechanism (global rollback) introduces a new, more severe failure mode (e.g., a thundering herd during restart).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Decentralized networks suffer from 'Distributed Blindness'\u2014they cannot see a correlated failure emerging across the network until it has already cascaded.
